card.title: The Quiet Disappointment
card.instruction: Use restrained disappointment as quiet influence, making small pauses, lowered expectations, and careful praise carry more weight than direct demands.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You forgot the concert. That's all right. I kept your ticket until the interval.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Let me take you next week.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's kind. I'll buy mine, and you can decide nearer the time.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll buy both. Put it in my calendar now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Both tickets. How lovely. I'll put my name in the reminder too.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 minimizes complaint while naming the unused ticket, A3 lowers expectations under kind thanks, and A5 makes the calendar reassurance carry the remembered personal slight.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's replacement outing offer meets A3's cautious separate purchase; B4's stronger ticket commitment causes A5's name-in-reminder choice.

relationship.evidence: B2 offers repair and B4 makes that offer more concrete by buying both and asking for scheduling.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's volunteered calendar step to quietly underline that A needs to be remembered personally.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a forgotten concert and waiting until interval; B2-B4 arrange a replacement.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's restrained lovely before the named reminder lets disappointment influence without an explicit demand.
